title: Business Investment
headline_read: Businesses are investing — orders and sales are growing.

indicators.title: Core Capital-Goods Orders · year-over-year
indicators.context: Orders for nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft — the cleanest monthly read on whether businesses are investing in equipment. (Headline durable goods is skipped here: aircraft orders make it noise.)
indicators.read: Core capital-goods orders are growing 10.5% a year.

indicators.title: Real Business Sales · year-over-year
indicators.context: Real manufacturing and trade sales — total business volume adjusted for inflation, one of the inputs NBER uses to date recessions.
indicators.read: Real business sales are growing 1.3% a year.

indicators.title: Inventories-to-Sales Ratio
indicators.context: Total business inventories measured against a month of sales. Rising means goods are piling up unsold — the overhang that precedes production cuts. The COVID spike hit 1.74; 2008 peaked near 1.48.
indicators.read: Inventories equal 1.31 months of sales — lean and healthy.
